Container.Name: Prusa-Connect
Container.Overview: Self-hosted local Prusa Connect server for managing Prusa 3D printers on your LAN without relying on Prusa's cloud. Uses Prusa Research's official Docker image. First-time setup is completed in the browser. This Unraid template is independently maintained and not officially maintained by Prusa Research.
Container.Requires: FIRST-TIME SETUP CODE: On initial startup, open this container's logs and find setup_code=XXXX-XXXX-XXXX. Enter the one-time code in the browser to claim administrator ownership. A restart before completing setup generates a new code. Restart the container after completing the first-run wizard. PORT: The default WebUI and printer API uses TCP 8080. If host port 8080 is taken (for example by qBittorrent or SABnzbd), change only the Host Port in the Unraid installer; the container port remains 8080. STORAGE: The official image runs as UID/GID 10001:10001, not PUID/PGID. BEFORE FIRST START: Unraid-created bind mount directories normally belong to UID/GID 99:100. Prusa runs as 10001:10001 and cannot write them until ownership is corrected. Review all actual host paths in the installer, create them and run chown -R 10001:10001 on those Prusa-only directories. Do not change unrelated appdata. In particular /config/config.d must be writable. This template cannot apply chown automatically; see README for exact instructions. The base /config/config.yaml is optional on first startup and is not bind-mounted by this template.

Config.Name: WebUI / API / Printer Port
Config.Description: Host TCP port for the web interface, REST API, and printer connections; container port is 8080.

Config.Name: Configuration and Database
Config.Description: Persistent writable authentication database, resource overlay, first-run settings and history. Must be owned by UID/GID 10001:10001 before first startup.

Config.Name: Storage
Config.Description: Uploaded print files and local storage.

Config.Name: Temporary Files
Config.Description: Writable scratch space required when the root filesystem is read-only.
